alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the ASV's connective *And* (rule 14); the verb takes the verb.
Inflected verb aligns to subject pronoun plus lexical verb, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Object marker H853 with no English word spent on the object relation; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Construct noun takes only its own English word; the relation is carried by the rectum's possessive rendering (rule 19).
Article on the rectum takes the phrase's single written *the*, which English fronts to the left edge of the anarthrously-rendered possessive (rule 29).
Rectum rendered attributively as an English possessive; the relation is written inside the word *people’s* (rules 19, 28).
Waw of the consecutive form takes *and* (rule 14).
Finite verb; the English carries no separate subject pronoun here, the subject of the preceding clause standing over it.
Object marker H853 with a bare English object; no word is spent on the object relation (rule 16).
Construct noun takes a supplied *the* plus its own word: the ASV renders the rectum arthrously, so nothing is fronted and the second *the* is the rectum's article's (rule 29).
Article on the rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word (rule 29, arthrous case).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19) and its two-word rendering; head on *sin*, the word carrying the lexeme, since *offering* is the supplied generic (rules 24, 31).
Written relative takes the ASV's *which*.
Verbless relative clause with a prepositional predicate: the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition heading the predicate, headed on the preposition (rules 20, 49).
Article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token and takes the written *the* (rule 12).
Noun takes its own word.
Waw takes *and* (rule 14).
Finite verb takes the lexical verb; the object pronoun belongs to the suffix (rule 18).
Object suffix takes the English object pronoun (rule 18).
Waw takes *and* (rule 14).

Denominative piel 'make a sin offering of' is rendered *offered ... for sin*: the whole expression is the verb's, discontinuous around the suffix's *it* (rule 25), and heads on *sin*, whose loss loses the lexeme while *offered* alone offers anything (rules 31, 44). The competing reading heads on *offered* as the English predicate; rule 44 forbids that preference.
Object suffix takes the English object pronoun (rule 18).
Preposition takes the written *as*; a second English word stands for the article and the adjective, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet.
Article assimilated into the pointed preposition takes the written *the* (rule 12).
Substantival adjective takes *first*; the ASV supplies no generic noun, so nothing further joins the unit (rule 31).

review_notes: Both object markers are unrepresented: the ASV writes each object bare and no English word is spent on the object relation (rule 16).

The two construct chains are counted separately by rule 29: קָרְבַּן הָעָם has one written *the*, which the rectum's article takes with the possessive rendering fronting it, while שְׂעִיר הַחַטָּאת is rendered arthrously with two *the*s, so nothing is fronted and the construct takes the supplied one.
The relative clause's לָ carries both the supplied copula and its own *for* under rule 49; the assimilated article beside it takes the written *the* under rule 12.
